For decades, competition between states was viewed primarily through military and political power. Today, economic tools have become instruments of strategy.
Sanctions, tariffs, export controls, critical minerals, and supply chains are shaping how countries compete, cooperate, and project influence.

In the first episode of The GSU Briefing, our Director, Ishan Jasuja, explains how geoeconomics has evolved into one of the defining forces shaping business and decision-making in today's world.
As geopolitical competition increasingly moves into the economic sphere, understanding these dynamics is no longer optional, it's essential.

snippet.title: Which Nations Truly Master Power? The Battle of Hard vs. Soft Influence
snippet.description:
Power shapes the world, but brute force alone isn’t enough anymore. Nations today blend military strength with cultural and economic influence—a strategy known as smart power. The U.S., China, Russia, and the EU all use different methods to dominate the global stage. Who does it best? And what happens when nations fail to strike the right balance?

In this video, we explore the fine line between hard power (force, military, coercion) and soft power (diplomacy, economy, culture) to uncover which countries have mastered the game of influence.
